bilingual.notes: No bilingual-education endorsement on the FY2026 OPI endorsement code list. Montana offers world-language endorsements (06A ARA/ASL/CHI/FRE/GER/IRI/ITA/LAT/RUS/SPA) and tribal-language endorsements (06Z ASB/BLA/CHE/CHI/CRE/CRO/DAK/GV/KOO/SAL), plus a separate Class 7 American Indian Language and Culture Specialist license, but these are language-content credentials, not bilingual-education credentials.

eld.notes: Endorsement code 06A ESL (English as a Second Language K-12), added to a Class 1 or Class 2 license per ARM 10.57.412. ARM 10.57.301 explicitly excludes ESL K-12 from the degree-major / portfolio / PRAXIS-only / National Board substitute pathway, so completion of an OPI-approved educator preparation program with supervised teaching experience is the operative pathway (program=true, practicum=true). The state rule does not specify a freestanding coursework-hour count or a required exam at the SEA-policy level; coded null per the project's ambiguity rule (absence-from-rule is not affirmative absence).

sei.notes: Montana does not require sheltered English instruction (SEI) training for all teachers. ARM 10.58.501 (Teaching Standards) requires educator preparation programs to address ELLs and diverse cultures and languages, but does not impose a universal in-service SEI mandate.

history.title: Indian Education for All Act enacted (HB 528, 1999)
history.description: The Montana Legislature enacted the Indian Education for All Act (HB 528, codified at MCA 20-1-501), implementing Article X § 1(2) of the Montana Constitution which commits the State to recognize "the distinct and unique cultural heritage of the American Indians" and to preserve their cultural integrity in its educational goals. IEFA requires every public school to teach about Montana's twelve federally-recognized tribes — and, after 2005 funding (HB 528 of 2005), the State funds districts on a per-pupil basis to support implementation. While not an EL credential per se, IEFA is the legal source of Montana's tribal-language and Native-American-Studies teacher pipelines and shapes how OPI frames cultural-competence elements of the educator-preparation standards (ARM 10.58.501).

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Montana's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: ARM 10.58.501 (Educator Preparation Standards) revised to enumerate ELL
history.description: Montana's revised educator preparation/teaching standards rule (ARM 10.58.501) explicitly names "English Language Learners (ELL)" within the diversity standard, replacing the 2014-era predecessor standards that did not enumerate ELL. Grounds the `professionalStandardsMentions.el: false → true` flip.

history.title: Montana Board of Public Education adopts Seal of Biliteracy
history.description: The Montana Board of Public Education adopted the Seal of Biliteracy in July 2021, authorizing districts to award the Seal to high school graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and one or more additional languages. Flips `sealOfBiliteracy.adopted` from null to true with `year: 2021`.
